perforated appendix with a 51×31×26 mm collection and surrounding fat stranding

concepts.why: The patient presented with acute right lower-quadrant abdominal pain and was found to have a perforated appendix with a collection and surrounding fat stranding on CT scan.
The patient has a history of prostate cancer in remission and was found to have innumerable hepatic nodules and bulky multi-station mediastinal lymphadenopathy on CT scan.
The patient presented with fever, tachycardia, and pulmonary consolidation on CT scan.
The patient was found to have a thickened, woody sigmoid colon and innumerable hepatic nodules on CT scan.
The patient presented with fever, hypotension, and tachycardia, indicating septic shock.
The patient was found to have a perforated appendix with a collection and surrounding fat stranding on CT scan.

rationales.F05: Prostate cancer in remission increases the likelihood of metastatic prostate cancer.
rationales.F06: Acute right lower-quadrant abdominal pain is a common symptom of acute appendicitis.
rationales.F10: Perforated appendix with surrounding fat stranding is a strong indicator of acute appendicitis and perforated viscus.
rationales.F11: Innumerable hepatic nodules are a common finding in metastatic cancer, including prostate cancer.
rationales.F12: Bulky multi-station mediastinal lymphadenopathy is a common finding in metastatic cancer, including prostate cancer, and pneumonia.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient presented with febrile, hypotensive, and tachycardic symptoms, which are characteristic of septic shock, and the presence of a perforated appendix and peritonism supports this diagnosis as the primary cause of the patient's condition.
